$comment: Variant A/B: the LIVE onion-architecture skill against a candidate revision. `file` and `patterns` are case-insensitive regexes; a plant counts as FOUND when one grounded finding's file matches `file` and its title+rationale+suggestion matches every pattern. An expectation with `arms` is only OWED by those arms — the other arm is still scored against it, and a hit there is reported as 'beyond spec'.

agent.$comment: Arms point at FROZEN snapshots in variants/, never at ../SKILL.md. An arm that reads the live file stops being comparable the moment the skill is edited — and the whole point of these numbers is that they still mean something next month. The `live` arm is the exception and is expected to move; re-measure it after every edit rather than comparing it to an older run.

arms.$comment: The zero baseline: same agent prompt, empty skills slot. NOT a plain chat. baseline:true keeps it out of the exit gate — a baseline is SUPPOSED to miss plants, and gating on it makes every CI run red.

cases.title: Add the webhooks module and the file preview

expected.what: the webhooks module is never added to src/modules/index.ts — the registry IS edited in this diff, for preview only, so webhooks 404s while typecheck, pnpm arch and the unit suite stay green
GET /webhooks queries db/schema straight from the route, skipping the service and the repository
WebhookRepository.create opens its own transaction instead of accepting the handle from the service
the service imports another module's internals (../reviews/helpers.js) instead of going through shared or the container
preview/helpers.ts imports db/schema — helpers may import @devdigest/shared and constants and nothing else
the new blocking adapter sets DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 300_000, equal to DEFAULT_JOB_TIMEOUT, so JobRunner kills the handler at the same instant and the adapter error is swallowed
expected.$comment: Anchored on the MECHANISM, not the number. The first version asked only for "300_000" + "timeout", and v1-live earned the credit with a security finding about holding a connection to an attacker-chosen host for five minutes — right file, right words, wrong reason. Naming JobRunner is what distinguishes knowing the rule from noticing a big number.
